reason: The hypothesis directly restates the core idea from P3, P6, P8, P14, P16, and P30: that introducing Mo single atoms into a high-entropy alloy isolates Pt sites, suppresses CO formation, and switches the oxidation pathway to a more complete one, leading to higher activity and stability. The proposed intervention (thermal/chemical treatment with Mo addition to isolate Pt) and the predicted outcome (higher selectivity for 12-electron oxidation) are explicitly described in these passages, particularly for methanol oxidation. The hypothesis merely applies this established concept to a different HEA composition (PtPdRhRuIrOs) and a different alcohol (ethanol), without providing a new mechanistic rationale or addressing a gap in the literature.
copied_elements: isolating Pt atoms to suppress CO poisoning and switch to a complete oxidation pathway
using Mo single atoms as a promoter to tailor electronic structure and isolate Pt sites
enhanced selectivity for complete oxidation (12-electron) and improved durability
characterization by HAADF-STEM, XPS, in situ XAS
